title: Load a settings file safely
description:
Write `load_settings(text, defaults)` that runs `text` (Lua assignments such as `width = 800`) in its **own** environment and returns a table of the settings:

- The environment starts empty except for `math` (so `height = math.floor(width * 0.75)` works).
- Afterwards, every key of `defaults` that the text did not set takes its default value.
- `math` itself is not part of the result.
- A syntax error or a runtime error returns `nil` and the error message.
- Nothing the text does may create real globals.

```lua
local s = load_settings("width = 1024\nfullscreen = true", { width = 800, height = 600 })
-- s.width == 1024, s.height == 600, s.fullscreen == true
```

solution.solution.lua:
function load_settings(text, defaults)
    local env = { math = math }
    local chunk, err = load(text, "settings", "t", env)
    if not chunk then
        return nil, err
    end
    local ok, run_err = pcall(chunk)
    if not ok then
        return nil, run_err
    end
    env.math = nil
    for key, value in pairs(defaults) do
        if env[key] == nil then
            env[key] = value
        end
    end
    return env
end

hints: `load(text, "settings", "t", env)` makes a function whose globals are fields of `env`. Run it with `pcall` so a runtime error comes back as a value.
unitTests:
test("settings and defaults", function()
    local s = load_settings("width = 1024\nfullscreen = true", { width = 800, height = 600 })
    check_eq(s, { width = 1024, height = 600, fullscreen = true })
    local t = load_settings("width = 1000\nheight = math.floor(width * 0.75)", {})
    check_eq(t.height, 750)
    check_eq(t.math, nil)
end)

test("no globals leak", function()
    load_settings("leaked = 1", {})
    check_eq(leaked, nil)
end)

test("errors", function()
    local s, err = load_settings("width = ", {})
    check_eq(s, nil)
    check(type(err) == "string")
    local t, err2 = load_settings("x = os.time()", {})
    check_eq(t, nil)
    check(err2:find("os") ~= nil, "the error should mention os")
end)
